gap: No result ChatGPT cited says that Lester's own FAQ answers 'Can I charge lithium batteries with a Summit II Charger?' this way: it uses the standard wet-cell (IEI) profiles and 'the maximum voltage is regulated by the lithium battery controller'. The same FAQ says Summit/E-Series chargers need about 15 VDC to start. So the Summit II, ChatGPT's 'Best premium' pick, depends on the battery's own controller to end charging, while LiTime's FAQ says only a charger with 0V activation can revive a pack whose BMS has shut off.
standout_why: Compared with the cited iwantgolf.com page (2026-08-13), the uncited #1 result canyonlakemobile.com (2026-04-25), and the cited Trojan OnePack PDF (downloaded, but its text could not be extracted, so not compared). iwantgolf covers this only in general terms: a pack may 'require a BMS enable signal or communication' and 'some chargers must detect battery voltage before activating'. It names no charger, threshold or mechanism. Canyon Lake says the Summit II 'stores 500+ profiles', is 'reprogrammable', and leaves lithium to the matching profile. It never says Lester's lithium answer is a wet-cell profile with the battery controller capping voltage, and it has no start-voltage figure. One caveat: ChatGPT did get the Lester FAQ as uncited result #10. The fact sat in its results, but neither its answer nor any cited page says it. That is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: This argues against ChatGPT's 'Best premium: Lester Summit II' for the usual shopper with an aftermarket drop-in 48V LiFePO4 pack. In Lester's own words, the Summit II charges lithium on a wet-cell profile and relies on the battery's controller (Summit II is CAN bus compliant) to cap voltage. It suits OEM or CAN-integrated lithium carts, not a generic pack whose BMS only disconnects. It also needs about 15 VDC at the terminals to start, so it cannot charge a pack whose BMS has opened after over-discharge. For a generic drop-in pack, a fixed 58.4 V LiFePO4 charger with 0V/activation mode (LiTime's line) is the safer fit. LiTime's FAQ says 'Chargers without 0V activation cannot activate' an over-discharged battery whose BMS has entered protection. I could not open LiTime's or Vatrer's product pages (HTTP 429), so whether each model has activation and the current prices are still unverified.

findings.label: How it charges lithium
findings.value: Uses the standard wet-cell (IEI) profiles; maximum voltage is regulated by the lithium battery controller
findings.source_title: Battery Charger FAQs & Troubleshooting - Lester Electrical
findings.note: FAQ entry 'Can I charge lithium batteries with a Summit II Charger?' Quoted answer: 'Yes, The standard Wet Cell battery profiles are used (IEI) and the maximum voltage is regulated by the lithium battery controller'. The E-Series II entry gives the same answer.

findings.label: CAN bus
findings.value: All Summit II chargers are CAN bus compliant
findings.source_title: Battery Charger FAQs & Troubleshooting - Lester Electrical
findings.note: FAQ 'Does my charger have CAN bus?' Answer: 'All Summit II Chargers are CAN bus compliant'. Taken with the lithium answer, the battery side has to do the voltage control.

findings.label: Minimum start voltage
findings.value: approx. 15 VDC (Summit and E-Series); Lestronic 2 needs 70% of rated voltage
findings.source_title: Battery Charger FAQs & Troubleshooting - Lester Electrical
findings.note: FAQ 'What if my batteries' voltage is too low, can they still be charged?' says 'There is a minimum start voltage for all Lester Chargers'. A lithium pack whose BMS has opened shows close to 0 V at the terminals, which is below this threshold (my inference).

findings.label: Charge lockout wire
findings.value: Blue wire drives an external lockout that keeps the vehicle from moving during a charge cycle
findings.source_title: Battery Charger FAQs & Troubleshooting - Lester Electrical
findings.note: Lester says to check the vehicle maker's documentation for this connection.

findings.label: Output at 48 V
findings.note: This page does not mention lithium or CAN. It says the Bluetooth app can select the active profile and upload new ones.

findings.label: Chargers without 0V activation cannot wake a BMS-protected pack
findings.value: 'Use a 0V LiFePO4 charger. Chargers without 0V activation cannot activate.'; 'most lead-acid chargers cannot activate lithium batteries.'
findings.note: FAQ 'Why does the battery fail to activate?' gives the root cause as 'Battery is over-discharged → BMS entered protection.' For 12 V packs the protection threshold is '<10V'. The FAQ gives no 48 V threshold.

findings.label: What activation is for
findings.value: Wakes BMS dormancy caused by over-discharge (12 V packs: below 10 V) and Bluetooth batteries that are powered off
findings.source_title: How to Wake Up a Lithium Battery - LiTime
findings.note: Article dated 2026-06-24. It refers to 'LiTime chargers' in general and names no model.
